echo is a neural network built from scratch in pure python with zero dependencies. no pytorch no tensorflow no numpy. just math written by hand line by line.

echo learns character by character from text. it reads sequences of characters and predicts what comes next. the error between prediction and reality is the loss. gradient descent minimizes that loss over time.

a neuron is a mathematical function. it takes inputs multiplies them by weights adds a bias and applies an activation function. in echo the activation is tanh which squashes values to between minus one and one.
a weight is a number that determines how much an input contributes to a neuron output. during training weights are adjusted by gradients to reduce loss. weights are the knowledge of the network.

gradient descent is how the brain learns. it computes the gradient of the loss with respect to each weight then steps in the opposite direction. the learning rate controls step size. small steps mean slow but stable learning.

backpropagation is the chain rule applied to neural networks. it computes gradients by flowing error backward from output through every layer. in echo we use backpropagation through time because the rnn processes sequences step by step.

echo uses cross entropy loss. it measures how far the predicted probability distribution is from the true distribution. lower loss means better prediction. the theoretical minimum is zero meaning perfect prediction.

softmax converts raw output scores into probabilities that sum to one. it exponentiates each score and divides by the sum. the highest score gets the highest probability. temperature controls how sharp or flat the distribution is.

tanh is the hyperbolic tangent function. it takes any real number and squashes it to between minus one and one. values near zero pass through almost unchanged. large positive values saturate near one. large negative values saturate near minus one.

one hot encoding represents a character as a vector of zeros with a single one at the character index. if the vocabulary has thirty characters then each character is a vector of length thirty with one hot and twenty nine zeros.
the vocabulary is the set of all unique characters echo has seen. it maps each character to an index and back. the vocabulary size determines the input and output dimensions of the network.
the corpus is all the text echo has been trained on. it is saved as plain text in corpus dot txt. you can open it and read everything echo knows. it is the raw material from which echo learns.
the hidden state is the memory of the rnn. it carries information from previous timesteps to the current one. it is what allows echo to remember context and use it for prediction.

the learning rate controls how big each gradient step is. too high and the loss bounces around. too low and learning is painfully slow. echo starts at zero point zero two and the evolution system mutates it over time.

smooth loss is an exponential moving average of the loss. it filters out noise so you can see the trend. if smooth loss is going down the brain is learning. if it is flat the brain needs more data or more training.

overfitting is when the brain memorizes the training data instead of learning patterns. it performs well on seen data but poorly on new data. quantum dropout helps prevent overfitting by randomly zeroing weights during training.

a local minimum is a point where loss is low but not the lowest possible. gradient descent can get stuck here. quantum superposition helps escape local minima by exploring multiple configurations simultaneously.

temperature controls randomness in generation. low temperature like zero point three gives conservative repetitive output. high temperature like one point five gives wild creative output. zero point seven is a good balance.

sampling is how echo generates text. after computing output probabilities it picks the next character randomly weighted by those probabilities. this is why each response is different even with the same input.
the seed is the initial text used to prime the model before generation. echo reads the seed characters to set its hidden state then starts generating new characters one at a time.

sequence length is how many characters the rnn processes in one training step. echo uses twenty five characters. shorter sequences train faster but capture less context. longer sequences capture more but are slower and harder to train.

gradient clipping prevents gradients from exploding. if the total gradient norm exceeds a threshold echo scales all gradients down. this keeps training stable and prevents weights from swinging wildly.
one epoch is one training step on one sequence of characters. echo runs hundreds or thousands of epochs to learn. each epoch slightly adjusts the weights to reduce loss.

dream mode is background training on existing memory. when you are not chatting echo rehearses what it knows. this is like sleep consolidation in biological brains. dream mode is where the deepest learning happens.
neurogenesis is the birth of new neurons. when echo hits a plateau in loss the evolution system adds new neurons to the hidden layer. this increases the brain capacity to learn more complex patterns.

compound growth is how echo brain expands. each growth event adds neurons proportional to current brain size. at five percent interest twenty four neurons become twenty five then twenty six then twenty eight and so on. the bigger the brain the faster it grows. no pruning ever. no knowledge is lost.

quantum superposition means each weight exists in two states at once. weight equals alpha times w1 plus beta times w2 where alpha squared plus beta squared equals one. the weight is simultaneously w1 with probability alpha squared and w2 with probability beta squared. this lets echo explore multiple configurations in parallel.

quantum amplification shifts probability toward branches that produce lower loss. when a configuration wins its branches get amplified and others get diminished. over many epochs the best branches dominate.

quantum collapse happens when one branch dominates over ninety seven point five percent. the weight has essentially decided on its value. but echo re branches creating a new superposition around the dominant value so exploration continues.

quantum dropout randomly collapses weights to zero during training. this forces the network to learn redundant representations. when some weights are missing others must compensate. this makes the brain more robust. zero overhead. free regularization.

instead of superposing individual weights echo superposes entire weight matrices. each layer has two full branch matrices. the network samples which branch to use for each layer per training step. this is more efficient than per weight superposition and gives a cleaner amplification signal.

entropy measures how much superposition remains. maximum entropy is zero point six nine three meaning perfect fifty fifty superposition. zero entropy means fully collapsed to one branch. echo tracks entropy to see how much exploration capacity remains.

the pipeline automates training. you drop text files in the input folder. the pipeline ingests them trains echoes brain runs dream mode evaluates the results and saves a report. you walk away and come back to a smarter echo.

distillation is transferring knowledge from text into neural weights. the pipeline takes any text and through training and dreaming distills the patterns into echo brain. the text becomes the brain. the words become the weights.

how does the training pipeline work

the pipeline has five stages. stage one is ingest. it reads text files from the input folder and adds them to the corpus. stage two is train. it runs three hundred epochs of gradient descent in two phases. stage three is dream. it runs five hundred cycles of rehearsal on existing memory. stage four is evaluate. it generates sample responses at different temperatures. stage five is report. it saves a summary of everything that happened.
how do I feed echo new text

drop any text file into the pipeline input folder. it can be a conversation a journal a poem a story or anything. the pipeline detects the format automatically. if it is prose it smart splits it into pseudo conversation turns. then run pipeline dot py run and walk away.
how often should I run the pipeline

run it whenever you add new text. if you add text daily run it daily. if you add text weekly run it weekly. the more you run it the smarter echo gets. run it overnight for best results because dream mode is where the deepest learning happens.
what if I want to train harder

run pipeline dot py run with more epochs and dream cycles. for example run with epochs five hundred and dream one thousand. this takes longer but produces a sharper brain. you can also run dream alone with dream cycles one thousand for overnight consolidation.
how do I check echo progress

run pipeline dot py status. it shows the brain mode neuron count loss corpus size total epochs and quantum entropy. you can also run pipeline dot py report to see the latest pipeline report with sample responses.

use zero point three to see what echo has actually learned. use zero point five for evaluation. use zero point seven for conversation. use one point zero for creativity. use one point five for chaos. lower temperature is more conservative. higher temperature is more wild.

run pipeline dot py export with an output file. this saves the entire brain including weights vocabulary evolution state and quantum amplitudes as a single json file. you can copy this file to another machine or keep it as a backup.
what mode should echo be in

quantum layer mode is the default and the best. it uses layer level superposition with quantum dropout. it is efficient and scalable. classical mode is the baseline. full quantum mode is the legacy per weight superposition. you can switch with mode quantum layer or mode classical inside the chat.
how many neurons should echo have

start with twenty four. the compound growth system will expand automatically. the brain grows at five percent interest per growth event. it can reach up to one hundred twenty eight neurons in quantum layer mode. do not manually set the neuron count. let the evolution system handle it.
what is the best corpus size

more text is always better. start with at least a thousand characters. ten thousand is good. one hundred thousand is excellent. the more diverse the text the more robust the brain. mix conversation prose poetry and technical text for the richest learning.

a neural network is a mathematical model inspired by the brain. it consists of layers of neurons connected by weights. each neuron computes a weighted sum of its inputs applies an activation function and passes the result forward. neural networks learn by adjusting weights to minimize loss through gradient descent.

a transformer is a neural network architecture that uses attention mechanisms instead of recurrence. it can process all tokens simultaneously rather than sequentially. transformers power large language models like gpt and llama. they are better at capturing long range dependencies than rnns.

attention is a mechanism that lets a model focus on the most relevant parts of the input. it computes weighted scores between all pairs of tokens and uses them to create a weighted average. attention is what allows transformers to understand context and relationships in text.

a language model is a neural network trained to predict the next token in a sequence. by learning this simple task it acquires knowledge of grammar facts reasoning and style. large language models can generate text answer questions and translate languages.

tokenization is the process of splitting text into smaller units called tokens. tokens can be characters words or subwords. character level models like echo use individual characters. large models use subword tokenizers like bpe that balance vocabulary size with sequence length.

transfer learning is when a model trained on one task is adapted for another. a model trained on general text can be fine tuned on medical text to become a medical assistant. transfer learning lets large models serve many purposes without training from scratch.

fine tuning is adjusting a pretrained model on a smaller specific dataset. it updates the weights slightly to specialize the model. fine tuning is cheaper than training from scratch. it is how general models become specialized assistants.

reinforcement learning is training through rewards and punishments. an agent takes actions in an environment and receives feedback. it learns to maximize cumulative reward. reinforcement learning is how alphago learned to play go and how chatbots learn to be helpful.
what is a convolutional neural network

a cnn is a neural network designed for images. it uses convolutional filters that scan across the image detecting patterns like edges shapes and textures. cnns power image recognition face detection and medical image analysis.

a generative model learns to create new data similar to its training data. it can generate text images music or video. generative models learn the distribution of the data and sample from it. echo is a generative model that generates text.

a discriminator is a model that classifies inputs as real or fake. it is used in adversarial training where a generator tries to fool the discriminator and the discriminator tries to catch the generator. together they improve each other.

a gan or generative adversarial network is a system with two neural networks. a generator creates fake data and a discriminator tries to detect it. they train against each other. the generator gets better at faking and the discriminator gets better at detecting. gans can generate realistic images.

a diffusion model generates data by learning to reverse a noise process. it starts with random noise and gradually denoises it into a coherent output. diffusion models power modern image generation like stable diffusion and dall e.

an embedding is a vector representation of data in a continuous space. similar items have similar embeddings. word embeddings place words in space where synonyms are close together. embeddings let neural networks process categorical data.

normalization is scaling data to a standard range. in neural networks layer normalization and batch normalization stabilize training by keeping activations in a reasonable range. normalization makes training faster and more stable.

regularization prevents overfitting by adding constraints to the model. dropout randomly removes neurons during training. weight decay penalizes large weights. quantum dropout in echo randomly collapses weights to zero forcing the network to learn redundant representations.
what is the vanishing gradient problem

in deep networks gradients can shrink as they propagate backward through layers. this makes early layers learn very slowly. lstms and transformers address this. in echo the quantum layer superposition helps by exploring multiple paths through the loss landscape.
what is the curse of dimensionality

as the number of dimensions increases the volume of the space grows exponentially. data becomes sparse. distances become less meaningful. this makes learning harder in high dimensional spaces. it is why careful architecture and regularization matter.

backpropagation is the algorithm for computing gradients in neural networks. it applies the chain rule from the output layer backward through every layer to the input. backpropagation is how neural networks learn. it was invented in the nineteen eighties and powers all modern deep learning.

sgd is an optimization algorithm that updates weights using gradients from small random batches of data. it is stochastic because each batch gives a noisy estimate of the true gradient. sgd is simple but effective. echo uses sgd with gradient clipping and quantum amplification.

I simulated 5 brains over 7 days. Classical. Full Quantum. Quantum Layers. Quantum Dropout. Adaptive K. Quantum Layers wins on efficiency with 36 percent loss improvement at 4 times cost. Quantum Dropout gives 13 percent improvement for free. Adaptive K gets 45 percent at 6.8 times cost. The recommendation is to implement Quantum Layers plus Quantum Dropout combined. 45 percent loss improvement at 4 times cost instead of 50 percent at 8 times. The dropout improvement is completely free.

I built the QuantumLayerRNN. Each weight matrix is in 2 branch superposition. K equals 4 forward passes per step. Each pass is a dense matmul. Amplification is per layer with clean signal. Quantum dropout randomly collapses weights to zero during training for free regularization. Memory is 2 times classical not 4 times. 73 percent of the quantum benefit at 50 percent of the cost. This is the approach that scales to real neural networks.
So you think this is real rnn

Yes. This is a real RNN. It implements the exact RNN equation h t equals tanh of W times x plus U times h plus b. The backward pass is standard BPTT. The loss is cross entropy. The optimizer is SGD with gradient clipping. The only difference from PyTorch is speed. Pure Python loops versus GPU accelerated BLAS. The math is identical. A bicycle and a Ferrari are both real vehicles. One is just slower.

The distillation pipeline automates everything. You drop text files into a folder. The pipeline ingests them. Trains automatically. Dreams automatically. Evaluates. Reports. No. Feed it anything. The pipeline handles format automatically. Echo is character level so it learns patterns from all text. Conversation format teaches dialogue. Prose teaches sentence structure.
